title: Monotonicity under increased noise
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $q,\rho,\sigma\in\mathbb{R}$ satisfy $q<1$ and $0\le\rho\le\sigma\le1$, and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be nonnegative. Then $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_q(T_\sigma f)$, where $T_\tau$ is the Fourier noise operator and $M_q$ is the extended power mean under the uniform measure.
replaced: Let $q<1$, $0\le\rho\le\sigma\le1$, and $f:\{0,1\}^n\to[0,\infty)$. Then $M_q(T_\rho f)\ge M_q(T_\sigma f)$. For nonnegative functions $u$, the extended mean is $M_r(u)=(\E u^r)^{1/r}$ when $r>0$; the same formula applies for $r<0$ when $u$ is positive everywhere. For positive $u$, $M_0(u)=\exp(\E\log u)$; if $r\le0$ and $u$ has a zero, $M_r(u)=0$. All expectations are uniform. For $d\in\mathbb N$, $h:\{0,1\}^d\to\bbr$, and $\tau\in\bbr$, the spectral noise operator is $T_\tau h(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq[d]}\tau^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x)=(-1)^{\sum_{i\in S}x_i}$ and $\widehat h(S)=\E[h\chi_S]$ under the uniform measure.
